To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we can: - Learn object transfiguration and attribute subspace from unpaired data - Generate novel images of people with specified eyeglass, smile, hair styles, lighting conditions etc. - Fine-grained control of image generation by swapping the projected component in attribute subspace

(1) we can learn object transfigurational attributes from unpaired data, (2) we can control the transfigurational attributes in a fine grained manner and (3) the learned transfigurational attributes are disentangled from background.
we can learn a subspace of attributes by adversarial training, and use it to perform object transfiguration on unpaired data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
learning a generative model of object attributes from unpaired images.
(1) Learning object transfiguration (2) Learning object attributes from unpaired data.
the problem of learning a mapping from a set of unpaired images, to a subspace that represents the attributes of the objects in the images, and then use the subspace for image transfiguration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present a novel method for learning object transfiguration, which is able to learn object attributes from weakly supervised data.
we propose a novel method that learns disentangled attributes subspaces from weak supervision and unpaired data, and can be applied to various image generation tasks.
we propose a novel generative model, which learns disentangled object subspaces from weak supervision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our work is the first to propose a deterministic GAN that can learn object disentanglement from unpaired data.
we can swap eyeglasses between two images, as shown in Fig. 3, or even swap hair styles between two images, shown in Fig.4.
we propose a new model that can learn a subspace for an attribute from unpaired data and can perform transfiguration of an object in one image by another object in another image.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to learn object transfigurations from unpaired data, and to do so without relying on feature space operations or appearance models.
it is possible to learn disentangled object attributes from weakly supervised training data, without the need for paired training data.

we can learn disentangled attribute spaces from weak supervision, which can be used for conditional image generation, and can also be used to learn appearance models for other downstream applications like image manipulation.
